answer: Anchor each agent identity to an e-passport chip: the NFC chip carries state-signed data verifiable against the issuing country public key directory, so one passport anchors one identity. An attacker wanting a tide of fake agents must obtain a tide of genuine passports, one per fake, instead of minting keys for free. The passport system acts as a trellis, giving honest agents one sturdy stem while duplicates are pruned at enrollment, and each rejection leaves a ripple in the audit log. The limit is access: people without passports need another path.
